results.update: This is a short file: the contractor sent a completed-roof supplement in mid-January, Joseph's office sent the supplement package back for review the same day it was requested, and the contractor confirmed it looked good. No correspondence has been found since January 21.
results.staleReason: Last email found is from January 21; the card was not touched again until February 18, which appears to be a Trello-side move rather than new correspondence — a narrowed search for this claim after January 21 turned up nothing further.

timeline.event: The contractor reported the roof work was complete and asked for the claim to be increased and depreciation released, sending the estimate, certificate of completion and photos.
Joseph's office sent the supplement package to the contractor for review.

results.update: The carrier is reviewing supplemental damage documentation submitted on September 8 and said it needs up to 14 days; it has not agreed to send this to appraisal, citing unresolved coverage and causation questions. An internal review on September 21 flagged that the supervisor who was escalated to in August still has not responded after 40+ days and recommended Joseph decide whether to call directly or escalate further.

timeline.event: The contractor's estimator sent the initial position for the roof and related damage to the carrier.
The carrier said the supplemental estimate was under review and requested additional supporting documentation.
The contractor's estimator submitted a detailed, itemized supplement request with a supporting photo report.
The carrier denied the supplement request in full.
Joseph's office sent the Appraisal Demand Letter to the carrier, formally invoking the appraisal process.
Joseph's office followed up with the homeowner for any updates from the carrier.
The homeowner reported the carrier had denied the claim and asked what other options were available.
Joseph's office sent follow-up letters to the carrier asking that an appraiser be named, noting the 20-day deadline had passed.
The carrier said the appraisal request was premature pending resolution of its supplement review with the contractor.
Joseph's office clarified it was authorized to speak on the contractor's behalf and asked the carrier to detail its concerns; the carrier restated its supplement denial reasons.
Joseph's office disputed the "premature" position, citing the missed appraisal deadline, and asked to speak with a supervisor.
The carrier provided a supervisor's name; Joseph's office repeatedly asked for a direct phone number without success.
The carrier formally denied the appraisal request over unresolved coverage and causation questions and requested more supporting damage photos.
The contractor sent the completed job photos and certificate of completion.
Joseph's office forwarded the supporting photos and completion certificate to the carrier.
The carrier reiterated its documentation requirements; Joseph's office replied that the files sent were all that were available.
The carrier acknowledged the submitted documentation and said it would need up to 14 days to review it.
Internal file review flagged that the escalated supervisor had not responded in over 40 days and recommended Joseph decide on next steps.

results.update: This Kansas file went through two rounds with the same contractor: an earlier claim was closed and re-opened in April, and the carrier ultimately denied it with no appraisal available in Kansas. Joseph's office sent an estimate and depreciation summary on April 15 for the contractor's review; no further correspondence has been found since.

timeline.event: The contractor referred the file, sharing job photos and asking for a supplement packet for the full roof under a partial approval in Kansas.
Joseph's office requested the carrier estimate, EagleView report, damage description, and homeowner contact information.
The contractor advised the original claim had been closed and a new claim was opened with the client.
The contractor shared new photos under the new claim and asked for Joseph's opinion; Joseph confirmed the damage looked storm-related.
The contractor asked Joseph to write up an estimate.
Joseph's office asked for the EagleView report and carrier estimate with roof measurements before starting.
The contractor replied that the carrier had denied the claim and that no appraisal was available in Kansas, providing a photo.
Joseph's office sent the estimate and depreciation summary for review.

results.update: This out-of-state claim was pulled from normal handling in April: after the carrier's appraisal response came back, Joseph decided it needs referral to a local attorney rather than further appraisal work, and had the file moved to the supplement board marked do-not-touch pending that referral.

timeline.event: The contractor reported an out-of-state claim had been denied, sending photos and the contractor's estimate.
